title: Router: disallow cross-region fallback when org/project is region-pinned (with guarded override)
author: Elena Popov
body:
Summary: This changes smart routing behavior to enforce data residency semantics when a residency policy pins a region (pinned_region or allowed_regions==[single]). If a request is pinned, the router will not select endpoints in other regions and will not cross-region fail over on capacity/health events. An explicit opt-in override allow_cross_region_fallback is introduced, guarded by feature flag residency_allow_cross_region_fallback_override, and only honored for enterprise tiers. Motivation: Residency enforcement requires deterministic in-region routing. Prior routing behavior could cross-region fallback during transient capacity events, which is unacceptable once a customer has pinned residency. This PR is part of Hosted data residency enforcement and pairs with gateway admission checks (ENG-2842) and audit logging (ENG-2844).

Behavior changes:
- If residency policy resolves to a pinned region, candidate pools are filtered to that region before scoring.
- Cross-region fallback is disabled by default for pinned requests (including retries).
- If allow_cross_region_fallback=true AND feature flag residency_allow_cross_region_fallback_override is enabled for the org, we allow cross-region selection but emit a routing decision tag and require an explicit decision reason.
- If pinned and no healthy capacity exists in-region, routing fails fast with a deterministic error reason (the gateway will map to RESIDENCY_CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE; this PR returns RouterDecision.DENY with reason=PINNED_REGION_NO_CAPACITY).
- Dedicated: respects the pinned region for reserved pools; will not fail over to a different Dedicated region unless override is enabled.
- Private/VPC: no change; policies are evaluated but router is expected to be single-region by deployment topology. We still attach decision metadata for consistency.

Implementation notes:
- New routing constraint object ResidencyConstraint injected into RouterContext from policy evaluator results (region, policy_id, source_scope).
- CandidateSet building now takes an optional hard_region_filter that is applied ahead of scoring.
- Retry path now reuses the same region constraint (prevents "retry drift" when the original attempt exhausted local capacity).
- Added structured log fields and tracing attributes: residency.pinned_region, residency.decision, residency.override_enabled, residency.override_requested.

Risk/mitigation:
- Risk: some customers currently rely on cross-region failover for availability. Mitigation: this only activates when a pinned residency policy is enabled; plus the explicit override remains available behind a feature flag for documented exceptions.
- Risk: noisy denial errors during initial rollout. Mitigation: routing denial reason is explicit and can be tracked; SRE alerting will key on decision_reason.

Testing:
- Unit tests cover candidate filtering, scoring invariants, retry behavior, and override gating.
- Added integration test harness for multi-region simulated pools verifying no cross-region selection when pinned.

Checklist: Added metrics/tags for observability; updated docs comments in routing module; ensured decision metadata contains policy_id and evaluated_region; ran router load tests with pinned traffic distribution.

Related:
- Linear: ENG-2843
- ADR pointers: region pinning policy model (ADR-042), gateway enforcement semantics (ADR-043)
- Follow-ups: wire router deny reason to gateway error mapping + audit event emission in ENG-2842/ENG-2844; consider per-project overrides vs org-only (product decision)
commits: router: add ResidencyConstraint and inject into RouterContext
router: apply hard region filter for pinned residency policies
router: disable cross-region fallback for pinned requests
router: add guarded override allow_cross_region_fallback (feature flag + tier gating)
tests: add pinned routing integration coverage + retry drift regression test
obs: add tracing attrs and structured log fields for residency routing decisions
conversation:
Mina Haddad (review): Can you confirm we filter before scoring? We should not even consider non-pinned regions when pinned_region is set, otherwise we risk accidental selection if weights regress. Also: what happens on retries (do we re-evaluate policy)?

Elena Popov (author): Yes — candidate_set now takes hard_region_filter applied prior to scoring. Retried attempts reuse the same ResidencyConstraint derived from the original request context; we intentionally do not re-evaluate mid-flight to avoid retry drift and to preserve deterministic behavior.

Ravi Menon (review): For the override, please ensure it is gated by both feature flag and org tier. Also add a log field that makes it obvious when we routed out-of-region by override vs by misconfig.

Elena Popov: Added gating: requires enterprise_tier=true AND FF residency_allow_cross_region_fallback_override enabled for org. Added tracing attrs residency.override_enabled + residency.override_requested and structured log field residency.override_mode=explicit.

Marcus Lin (security review): We should treat cross-region fallback under pinned policy as a compliance event. Even if we allow override, we need evidence. Does this PR emit audit events?

Elena Popov: This PR does not emit audit events directly (router currently only tags telemetry). ENG-2844 will emit audit events using these tags + gateway decision context. I added policy_id + evaluated_region into RouterDecision metadata to make the audit event payload complete.

Sean Gallagher (SRE): For capacity exhaustion in a pinned region, is the error path deterministic? We need to alert on it and not confuse it with generic 5xx routing failures.

Elena Popov: Yes — the router returns RouterDecision.DENY with reason=PINNED_REGION_NO_CAPACITY. Gateway will map to a residency-specific error code; meanwhile we also increment a router metric (separate PR) based on decision reason.

Brian Murphy (API ergonomics): +1 on deterministic. Small request: rename reason PINNED_REGION_NO_CAPACITY vs REGION_PINNED_NO_CAPACITY for consistency with other enums.

Elena Popov: Renamed to RESIDENCY_PINNED_NO_CAPACITY and updated tests.

CI note: Initial run failed on lint due to unused enum import in retry_policy.ts; fixed in 4a9b2d1 and re-ran.

Final approvals: Mina Haddad approved; Ravi Menon approved; Marcus Lin approved (security); Sean Gallagher approved (SRE). Merged via squash.
release_notes: Routing now enforces pinned residency by preventing cross-region fallback when region pinning policies are active. A guarded org-level override (feature-flagged) can explicitly permit cross-region fallback for approved exceptions.
